title: カエルの為に鐘は鳴る
title_romaji: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru
sources: The harness alone, from the game's cartridge on mGBA (docs/first-script.md): no reader's snapshots, no memory written, no play outside the harness. The cartridge and snaps were studied outside it

From scratch: `entered` on the naming screen gave the name's kana codes (another set than the story's). find_relative, advancing (unit 1 and 2) and rom-font --find found nothing: the script is packed in the cartridge and drawn in a proportional font into fresh tiles

Found offline in snaps taken every frame from the press that starts a page: a word on the stack pointing at the page, unpacked whole into work RAM as numbers of its own, and beside it each number's code in the game's font

The table: the kana by one plan read off the first two pages' codes (hiragana from 0x000, katakana from 0x050, each with its small, voiced and half-voiced ones after), the small ones' order corrected by later pages; 100 kana codes on the bar's pages all fit it.
The signs, digits and 21 kanji were read in play, a page's codes beside its picture
Played from the naming through the opening duel, an old servant's news and the shore: three stretches, each replayed from a state with the script loaded
What the script said agreed with the rows read off 36 of 36 pictures, over 3 scenes. No screen without text was among them
The signs and kanji were read off the same pictures the comparison holds the script to; the kana plan was not, past the first two pages
notes: Read by the script games/gb/GB-7F805941.lua: a page of the window or a speech bubble, once it has begun to type and stands, from the page unpacked in work RAM through its list of codes. Not read: who speaks, pages of big letters (a laugh in the opening), the naming screen, menus and status rows. Kanji not met in play come out as U+FFFD.
